title: Base change of a relative global complete intersection
statement: Let $\rho:R\to R'$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $n,c\ge0$ integers, $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and let $f'_1,\dots,f'_c\in R'[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be their images under the ring map $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to R'[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ which applies $\rho$ to the coefficients and sends $x_j\mapsto x_j$. Put $S=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ and $S'=R'[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f'_1,\dots,f'_c)$. Then (a) the homomorphism of $R'$-algebras $S'\to R'\otimes_RS$ with $x_j\mapsto1\otimes(x_j\bmod(f_1,\dots,f_c))$ is an isomorphism; (b) if $S=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection], then $S'=R'[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f'_1,\dots,f'_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection over $R'$.

proof.text: (Part (a).) Write $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, $P'=R'[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $\kappa:P\to P'$ the coefficient map along $\rho$, so $f'_j=\kappa(f_j)$, and $\pi:P\to S=P/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ the quotient map, a surjective $R$-algebra homomorphism with kernel $(f_1,\dots,f_c)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-base-change] (with $A=S$, $m=c$, this $\pi$ and $R\to R'$ the map $\rho$) the $R'$-algebra homomorphism $\pi':P'\to S\otimes_RR'$, $x_j\mapsto\pi(x_j)\otimes1$, is surjective with kernel $(f'_1,\dots,f'_c)$; hence it induces an isomorphism of $R'$-algebras $S'=P'/(f'_1,\dots,f'_c)\xrightarrow{\sim}S\otimes_RR'$. Composing with the swap $S\otimes_RR'\to R'\otimes_RS$, $s\otimes r'\mapsto r'\otimes s$ (an isomorphism of rings, $R'$-linear for $r'\mapsto 1\otimes r'$ on the left and $r'\mapsto r'\otimes1$ on the right), gives the isomorphism of $R'$-algebras $S'\to R'\otimes_RS$, $x_j\mapsto1\otimes\pi(x_j)$, of (a). (Source: proof of 00SS, '$R'\otimes_RR[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)=R'[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$'.)

proof.text: (The residue field extension.) For (b), fix a prime $\mathfrak p'\subset R'$ and put $\mathfrak p=\rho^{-1}(\mathfrak p')$, a prime of $R$. Let $\pi_{\mathfrak p}:R\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $\pi_{\mathfrak p'}:R'\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ be the maps to the residue fields [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra] (a), $\ker\pi_{\mathfrak p'}=\mathfrak p'$; so the ring map $\phi=\pi_{\mathfrak p'}\circ\rho:R\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ has kernel $\rho^{-1}(\mathfrak p')=\mathfrak p$, and for $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$, $\phi(s)\neq0$ is a unit of the field $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra] (d) there is a ring map $\lambda:\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ with $\lambda\circ\pi_{\mathfrak p}=\pi_{\mathfrak p'}\circ\rho$. Thus $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is a field extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ via $\lambda$ [def-pc-field-extension], and the two $R$-algebra structures on $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$, through $R'$ and through $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, coincide.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SS (line 36639), proof of (1), line 36658: the fibre of the base change over $\mathfrak p'$ is a base change of the fibre over $\mathfrak p$ along $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\subset\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ (left implicit in the source)

proof.text:
(The fibre of $S'$ is a field extension of the fibre of $S$.) Keep step 2 and let $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $F'=S'\otimes_{R'}\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ be the fibre rings [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; write $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $K=\kappa(\mathfrak p')$. There are ring isomorphisms
$$F'\cong K\otimes_{R'}S'\cong K\otimes_{R'}(R'\otimes_RS)\cong K\otimes_RS\cong K\otimes_k(k\otimes_RS)\cong K\otimes_kF:$$
the first and last by the swaps $a\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes a$; the second is $K\otimes_{R'}-$ applied to the $R'$-algebra isomorphism of step 1; the third is [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] with its $R\to S$ the map $\rho:R\to R'$, its $A=K$ (an $R'$-algebra via $\pi_{\mathfrak p'}$) and its $B=S$, where $K$ is an $R$-algebra via $\pi_{\mathfrak p'}\circ\rho$; the fourth is the inverse of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] with its $R\to S$ the map $\pi_{\mathfrak p}:R\to k$, its $A=K$ (a $k$-algebra via $\lambda$) and its $B=S$, where $K$ is an $R$-algebra via $\lambda\circ\pi_{\mathfrak p}$, which is the same $R$-algebra structure by step 2. A ring isomorphism $\varphi:A_1\to A_2$ gives the bijection $\mathfrak P\mapsto\varphi(\mathfrak P)$ of prime ideals, which preserves the closed sets $V(J)$, hence a homeomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}A_1\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_2$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; so by [lem-weil-pbc-homeomorphism-krull-dimension] $\dim\operatorname{Spec}F'=\dim\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_kF)$. Moreover, if $F=0$ then $K\otimes_kF=0$ (every $a\otimes b=a\otimes0=0$), so $F'=0$; that is, $F'\neq0$ implies $F\neq0$.

proof.text: (The fibre of $S$ is of finite type over $k$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-base-change] applied to $\pi:P\to S$ (step 1) and the ring map $\pi_{\mathfrak p}:R\to k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, the $k$-algebra homomorphism $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to S\otimes_Rk=F$, $x_j\mapsto\pi(x_j)\otimes1$, is surjective, $F$ being a $k$-algebra via $\mu\mapsto1\otimes\mu$. Hence $F$ is a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SS (line 36639), proof of (1), lines 36660-36662; the finite type hypothesis of Lemma Tag 00P3 (line 28290)

proof.text: (Conclusion of (b).) Assume $S=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection], and let $\mathfrak p'\subset R'$ be a prime with $F'=S'\otimes_{R'}\kappa(\mathfrak p')\neq0$; let $\mathfrak p,k,K,\lambda,F$ be as in steps 2-3. By step 3, $F\neq0$, so by the definition $\dim\operatorname{Spec}F=n-c$. By step 4, $F$ is a finite type $k$-algebra, and $K/k$ is a field extension via $\lambda$ (step 2), so [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-preserved-field-extension] gives $\dim\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_kF)=\dim\operatorname{Spec}F=n-c$, and by step 3 $\dim\operatorname{Spec}F'=n-c$. Since $\mathfrak p'$ was arbitrary and $S'=R'[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f'_1,\dots,f'_c)$ has $n$ variables and $c$ equations, $S'$ is a relative global complete intersection over $R'$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. (Source: proof of 00SS, 'By Lemma 00P3 the fibres of a base change have the same dimension as the fibres of the original map ... Thus (1) follows'.)
